purpose: The one screen I open first. A single verdict for the close I am being asked to attest to, and if the answer is no, the named blocker.
layout_hints: Hero verdict card (green/red) with the IsAttestationReady column and, beneath it, a blocker list. Right rail: assurance grade summary. Nothing below the fold that is not a blocker.
name: Can I Sign? — /cfo/attestation

purpose: Every reason I cannot sign yet, each one traced to the row that produced it.
layout_hints: Ordered list, most severe first. Each row: the blocking condition, the entity it fires on, and a link into that entity's detail route. Empty state must say 'no blockers' explicitly, never render blank.
name: Blockers — /cfo/attestation/blockers

purpose: When the verdict reads TRUE, what proportion of the controls behind that TRUE were actually demonstrated to work — versus asserted by an interested party, versus never exercised at all.
layout_hints: Three-band stacked bar: demonstrated / asserted / never-exercised. Below it, the per-control table that produced the bands. The headline number is the grade, not the verdict.
name: Assurance Grade — /cfo/assurance/grade

purpose: The requirements I am personally attesting to that have no computed witness — and the named human who would answer for each if it failed.
layout_hints: Table: requirement, blocking?, has-witness?, accountable human, their role. Rows with no witness AND blocking are the emphasis. Each row links to the requirement detail.
name: Controls Nobody Watches — /cfo/assurance/unwitnessed

purpose: Every control claim in this model that rests on a human typing a conclusion rather than on something computed.
layout_hints: Two-column split: computed claims vs typed claims, with counts. The typed side is the working list. Each entry shows who typed it and when.
name: Typed, Not Computed — /cfo/assurance/typed-conclusions

purpose: Across the whole close, is there any independent human observation at all — or is every layer the same handful of people confirming each other?
layout_hints: Chain/graph view: approvals and verification outcomes as nodes, edges where one person confirms another. Self-witnessed loops highlighted. Sidebar counts independent vs self-witnessed.
name: Who Witnessed the Witnesses — /cfo/assurance/independence

purpose: For every approval in this close, the human who was personally accountable — and whether an exception routed authority away from the person who normally holds it.
layout_hints: Table per approval: approver, role held at the time, normal holder, exception invoked?. Rerouted rows flagged. Links to the exception invocation detail.
name: Who Held Authority — /cfo/authority/accountability

purpose: My approval on se-close06 — is there anything behind it other than the fact that I clicked approve?
layout_hints: Detail card per approval I gave: what was verified, by whom, with what evidence. An approval with nothing behind it is rendered as a warning state, not an empty section.
name: My Own Approvals — /cfo/authority/my-approvals

purpose: The full set of controls, versions, and evidence records my signature actually depends on — the blast radius of my own name.
layout_hints: Dependency tree rooted at the attestation, expanding into controls, versions, evidence. Each node shows its current state. This is the reference view the change-watch route diffs against.
name: What My Signature Rests On — /cfo/attestation/dependencies

purpose: Since the moment I signed, has anything changed that would have altered my decision — specifically touching a control, a version, or an evidence record my signature depended on.
layout_hints: Timeline diff anchored at the signature timestamp. Only changes intersecting the dependency set are shown; unrelated churn is explicitly excluded and the exclusion is stated.
name: Changed Since I Signed — /cfo/attestation/changed-since

purpose: If I re-run every attestation column against this same data six months from now, will it give the same answer? Name every column whose value depends on when it is read.
layout_hints: Table of attestation columns with a tense-dependent flag, sourced from the EvaluationContexts modelled instant. Time-dependent columns get an explicit warning band at the top.
name: Would It Survive Restatement — /cfo/assurance/restatement

purpose: One execution, everything I would be signing for it.
layout_hints: Full-page record: execution header, per-step conformance, control results, evidence links. Reachable from the blocker list and the home verdict.
name: Attestation Detail — /cfo/attestation/execution/:executionId

purpose: Every close control at a glance: which fired, which held, and which are structurally incapable of failing.
layout_hints: Grid of control tiles, each showing bound steps, witness presence, and whether it has ever produced a negative. Inoperative controls are visually distinct, not just sorted lower.
name: Control Board — /controller/controls

purpose: Which of my blocking close controls are structurally incapable of failing — declared, bound to a step, and yet with no mechanism that could ever produce a negative result.
layout_hints: List with a three-state badge per control: has-witness / witness-ever-fired / could-ever-fire. The third state is the finding. Each row explains WHY it cannot fire.
name: Inoperative Controls — /controller/controls/inoperative

purpose: For each control with a witness, is the witness evaluated at the same steps where the control is bound? req-close-evidence is bound to close-03 and close-08 — is its witness scoped to both?
layout_hints: Two parallel columns per control: steps bound vs steps witnessed, with the set difference called out. A non-empty difference is the finding.
name: Witness Scope vs Binding — /controller/controls/witness-scope

purpose: Did the same agent both prepare and approve any part of this close — computed, not asserted. And could it even have happened, or is the control passing because the structure never gave it the chance to fail?
layout_hints: Top: the computed verdict. Below: the opportunity analysis — executions where the same agent COULD have held both seats. A pass with zero opportunity is rendered as inconclusive, not green.
name: Separation of Duties — /controller/controls/separation-of-duties

purpose: One number per close: did the execution actually conform to its procedure version, and if not, how far off was it?
layout_hints: Reuse the existing spec/execution ledger layout. Add a single conformance score in the header. Divergent steps anchor-linked from the score.
name: Spec vs Execution — /controller/execution/conformance

purpose: For each divergence, was there a governing instrument behind it — an invoked exception, an approved change request, a recorded deviation with an owner — or did the run simply do something different and nobody wrote it down?
layout_hints: Per divergence: the instrument that covers it, or an explicit 'ungoverned' state. Ungoverned rows are the working list and sort first.
name: Divergence Nobody Governed — /controller/execution/ungoverned-divergence

purpose: Every approval on this close — was it given by an agent who actually held the required role AT THE TIME they approved, not just someone who holds it today?
layout_hints: Timeline per approval: the assignment window vs the approval instant. Approvals outside their window are the finding. Bitemporal — do not compare against today.
name: Authority at Time of Approval — /controller/authority/validity

purpose: Did any AI agent or automated pipeline execute a step that requires human confirmation, or sign off on something a human was supposed to own?
layout_hints: Table of software-executed steps against their human-confirmation requirement. Include an explicit 'never approached' column — an untested boundary is not a passing one.
name: Machine Did Human Work — /controller/authority/ai-boundary

purpose: Three satisfaction records are asserted-only. For each: who asserted it, did they have any independent basis, and were they the same person who executed the step they were scoring?
layout_hints: Per record: asserter, executor, independence verdict. Same-person rows flagged. Evidence URI shown or its absence stated explicitly.
name: Asserted, Not Demonstrated — /controller/evidence/asserted

purpose: One control, end to end: what it says, where it is bound, what witnesses it, and every time it has been evaluated.
layout_hints: Detail page. Header with the statement and blocking flag; sections for bindings, witness, and evaluation history. This is the shared requirement detail specialised for the controller.
name: Control Detail — /controller/controls/requirement/:requirementId

purpose: The steps I personally executed, and whether each one closed cleanly or closed past something.
layout_hints: Card per step execution with status, duration vs expected, and blocking-control state. Anything that closed past a blocking control is the emphasis.
name: My Steps — /finance-analyst/my-work

purpose: On the steps I personally executed, did any close out while a BLOCKING requirement was still not fully satisfied?
layout_hints: List of my step executions with an unmet blocking control, each showing the control and its satisfaction level. This is a personal-exposure screen — keep it short and unambiguous.
name: Closed Past a Control — /finance-analyst/my-work/blocking-unmet

purpose: Which blocking requirements were attached to a step I ran but never got a satisfaction record at all — not satisfied, not unsatisfied, just never assessed.
layout_hints: The absence IS the finding, so render missing records as explicit rows, never as an empty table.
name: Never Assessed — /finance-analyst/my-work/never-evaluated

purpose: Which of my steps ran long without anybody recording why — and of those, which had an exception available that nobody invoked.
layout_hints: Table: step, actual vs expected, deviation recorded?, exception available?, exception invoked?. The available-but-not-invoked combination is the finding.
name: Late and Unexplained — /finance-analyst/my-work/late-unexplained

purpose: For every step I ran that had a declared verification, did anybody actually perform it and record the observed signal — or did I just get a PASS with nothing behind it?
layout_hints: Per step: declared verification, observed signal or its absence, who observed. A PASS with no observation is rendered as hollow, not green.
name: Declared vs Performed — /finance-analyst/evidence/verification-performed

purpose: On the steps I ran, was the person who observed the passing signal ever me — and when it was, did I at least attach an evidence URI?
layout_hints: Self-witness table scoped to my steps: observer, is-me flag, evidence URI present. Self-witnessed with no URI is the weakest state and should read that way.
name: My Own Evidence Quality — /finance-analyst/evidence/my-evidence

purpose: When I attested my reconciliation, was the underlying ledger data actually fresh — or was I certifying against a source that had already gone stale under its own SLA?
layout_hints: Per binding: freshness SLA, age at run, authoritative flag. Judged against the modelled instant, never the wall clock.
name: Was My Source Fresh — /finance-analyst/evidence/source-freshness

purpose: Was the source stale AT THE MOMENT I RAN, or has it merely gone stale since — and are those the same steps?
layout_hints: Two-column comparison: staleness at run-time vs staleness at the current evaluation context. The delta between the columns is the whole point of the screen.
name: Stale Then vs Stale Now — /finance-analyst/evidence/stale-then-vs-now

purpose: Of the executions that ARE clean, how many are clean because everything was checked and passed, versus clean because there was almost nothing checking them?
layout_hints: Scatter or two-axis table: controls-checked against controls-passed. Low-check/high-pass is the quadrant of interest and should be labelled as such.
name: Clean, or Just Unchecked — /finance-analyst/quality/clean-but-uncovered

purpose: How many of the blocking controls that cleared me have NEVER produced a negative outcome anywhere in this model — and were any of my steps cleared ONLY by controls of that kind?
layout_hints: Per step: clearing controls, each tagged with whether it has ever fired negative. A step cleared exclusively by never-fired controls is the headline finding.
name: Cleared by a Mute Control — /finance-analyst/quality/cleared-by-mute-control

purpose: Of the blocking controls attached to the steps I run, how many have no computed witness — and is HasComputedWitness even telling me the truth, given a human typed it in by hand?
layout_hints: Coverage bar plus a caveat band: the declared-vs-actual witness comparison, because the declaration itself is a typed field and must be shown as such.
name: Coverage of My Controls — /finance-analyst/quality/witness-coverage

purpose: Everything currently live under my name: policy versions, knowledge claims, and the decisions waiting on me.
layout_hints: Three-panel dashboard: owned versions, owned claims (with approval state), pending decisions with age. Unapproved-but-live claims are the emphasis.
name: What I Own — /hr-policy-owner/ownership

purpose: Which claims am I the owner of that were never approved — and are any of them routing real cases right now?
layout_hints: List of owned fragments by status, with an 'operationally live' flag. Reviewed-but-not-Approved AND live is the finding.
name: Unapproved in My Name — /hr-policy-owner/ownership/unapproved

purpose: How many steps, exceptions and authority boundaries currently depend on a claim I have not signed, and how long has it been sitting at Reviewed?
layout_hints: Dependency fan-out from one fragment: steps, exceptions, boundaries. Header carries the age at Reviewed. This is the screen that makes an unsigned claim feel expensive.
name: Blast Radius of a Claim — /hr-policy-owner/ownership/blast-radius/:fragmentId

purpose: What decisions are waiting on me personally, and how long have they been waiting.
layout_hints: Queue ordered by age. Each item shows what it blocks downstream, so the cost of my delay is visible from the queue itself.
name: Waiting On Me — /hr-policy-owner/backlog

purpose: The full chain from my inbox outward: which knowledge gaps stay open because I have not decided, which steps sit downstream, and how many days of that delay are mine personally.
layout_hints: Chain view: my pending decision → blocked gap → downstream steps. Attribute delay days to me vs to the process explicitly; do not conflate them.
name: What My Delay Blocks — /hr-policy-owner/backlog/downstream

purpose: How many decisions have I made that the model still displays as outstanding against me? I cannot show what I have actually cleared.
layout_hints: Decision history with the terminal-state problem surfaced: Approved requests still counted open are flagged as a model defect, not hidden.
name: What I Have Cleared — /hr-policy-owner/backlog/my-decisions

purpose: kf-policy-ai-boundary says AI may draft but may not create legal commitments. Is that boundary actually being held?
layout_hints: Per boundary: assigned agent, executions, and whether a violation was possible. Pair every 'no violation' with an 'ever approached' count — the two together are the real answer.
name: Is the AI Boundary Held — /hr-policy-owner/governance/ai-boundary

purpose: Is the policy I own now resting on knowledge older than the policy itself has been reviewed?
layout_hints: Timeline: elicitation dates, version issue date, review cadence, next due. The comparison between knowledge age and review interval is the headline.
name: Knowledge Half-Life — /hr-policy-owner/governance/knowledge-half-life

purpose: Somebody's assignment ended. Did anything they owned or sourced go with them — claims, gaps, pending decisions — or did the departure genuinely leave nothing behind?
layout_hints: Per departed assignment: everything sourced or owned by that agent, with current ownership state. Orphaned items are the finding.
name: What Departed With Them — /hr-policy-owner/governance/departed-holders

purpose: If an employee disputes what they received, can I show that what was sent matched what I approved?
layout_hints: Per delivery: approved text vs transmitted text, side by side, with the approval record and date. A mismatch is the finding; identical is stated explicitly.
name: What Was Actually Sent — /hr-policy-owner/delivery/what-was-sent

purpose: The four gates I care about — consent, quiet hours, legal review, retention — each as a pass/fail with the breaching rows named.
layout_hints: Four gate tiles across the top; a breach list beneath whichever is selected. A gate with zero breaches must distinguish 'checked and clean' from 'never evaluated'.
name: Compliance Gates — /employment-counsel/compliance

purpose: Did we send an SMS to any recipient who had not given SMS consent at the moment we sent it?
layout_hints: Per SMS delivery: recipient, consent state at send time, verdict. Bitemporal — consent today is not the question.
name: SMS Without Consent — /employment-counsel/compliance/consent

purpose: Did any SMS go out between 20:00 and 08:00 in the recipient's own local time?
layout_hints: Per delivery: send instant, recipient timezone, local hour, verdict. Show the local-time conversion explicitly — the timezone is the whole difficulty.
name: Quiet Hours — /employment-counsel/compliance/quiet-hours

purpose: Did any message go out before my legal review of the underlying policy version was actually complete?
layout_hints: Timeline per campaign: review completion vs first transmission. Sends preceding review completion are the finding.
name: Sent Before My Review — /employment-counsel/compliance/legal-review

purpose: Do we still hold the exact text of every message we sent, for the full 2555-day retention period the policy commits us to?
layout_hints: Per delivery: text retained?, retention deadline, days remaining. Missing text is a breach and must render as one.
name: Retention Evidence — /employment-counsel/compliance/retention

purpose: For every recipient we could not reach, did we correctly refrain from marking their acknowledgement complete?
layout_hints: Per unreachable recipient: delivery state, acknowledgement state. An acknowledgement on an unreachable recipient is the finding.
name: Unreachable, Not Acknowledged — /employment-counsel/compliance/unreachable

purpose: For this policy run: who we meant to reach, who we actually reached, and where the rest went.
layout_hints: Funnel across the top (intended → sent → delivered → acknowledged), with each drop-off clickable into the rows that fell out.
name: Campaign Board — /communications-manager/delivery

purpose: Of everybody the pipeline intended to contact, what fraction actually received it — and where exactly did the rest go?
layout_hints: Sankey or stepped funnel with an explicit terminal bucket for every loss: refused, bounced, suppressed, deferred. No row may vanish without a bucket.
name: Approval-to-Delivery Yield — /communications-manager/delivery/yield

purpose: How many recipients are sitting in a bounced or failed state that nobody is working?
layout_hints: Worklist, not a report: each failed delivery with age and owner. Unowned failures sort first.
name: Bounced and Unworked — /communications-manager/delivery/failed

purpose: Was every template we actually sent approved by me — the ApprovalRole the policy names — before it went out?
layout_hints: Per sent template: approval record, approver role, approval instant vs send instant. Sends preceding approval are the finding.
name: Approved Before Sending — /communications-manager/governance/approval-authority

purpose: Has any template been edited since I approved it, and did we send the edited version under cover of my old approval?
layout_hints: Per template: approval timestamp, last edit timestamp, sends after the edit. Edit-then-send-on-old-approval is the finding.
name: Edited After I Approved — /communications-manager/governance/template-drift

purpose: For a message we sent last month, can I still show what I approved — the exact text, the exact approval, on the exact date — without that answer changing the next time somebody edits the template?
layout_hints: Immutable snapshot view: the text as sent, the approval as given. Must read from the frozen delivery record, never from the live template.
name: Freeze What I Approved — /communications-manager/governance/frozen-approval/:deliveryId

purpose: Did every SMS we actually transmitted carry the approved opt-out text?
layout_hints: Per SMS: transmitted text, opt-out present?. Missing opt-out is a breach row.
name: Opt-Out Text — /communications-manager/compliance/optout

purpose: Did any SMS we sent exceed 160 characters or split into more than 3 segments?
layout_hints: Per SMS: character count, segment count, both against their limits. Show the computed integer, not a re-derived length.
name: Oversized SMS — /communications-manager/compliance/sms-limits

purpose: One acknowledgement out of six deliveries. Is that because employees ignored us, or because the messages that landed were the least likely to be answered — wrong channel, wrong template, sent into the small hours?
layout_hints: Cross-tab of acknowledgement rate by channel, template, and send hour. The point is to separate audience apathy from our own targeting.
name: Why Nobody Answered — /communications-manager/audience/engagement

purpose: When we correctly refused to reach somebody, did anyone ever go back and reach them another way — or does 'correctly refused' quietly mean 'never communicated with again'?
layout_hints: Per suppressed recipient: the refusal reason, and any subsequent successful contact on another channel. No follow-up is the finding.
name: Correctly Refused, Then Forgotten — /communications-manager/audience/suppression

purpose: When the pipeline refused to send, was it refusing on a rule I set — or overriding an authorization I had already given, for a reason nobody routed back to me?
layout_hints: Per refusal: the governing rule, its owner, and whether it contradicts a standing authorization of mine. Contradictions are the finding.
name: Refused, or Overridden — /communications-manager/governance/authorization-override

purpose: Before I execute anything: am I authorized, are my inputs fresh, and did my last run leave a mess.
layout_hints: Four go/no-go tiles (authority, inputs, prior run, controls) resolving to a single may-I-run verdict. Built for a supervisor watching the agent as much as for the agent.
name: Pre-Flight — /close-automation/readiness

purpose: Is my own role assignment currently valid, and is the agent named in that assignment actually me?
layout_hints: Assignment card: validity window, named agent, identity match. An identity mismatch must halt, not warn.
name: Am I Authorized — /close-automation/readiness/authority

purpose: Before I extract: is every operational binding this step reads inside its freshness SLA, and is it the authoritative one?
layout_hints: Per binding: age, SLA, authoritative flag. Two independent failure modes — stale, and non-authoritative — must not be collapsed into one badge.
name: Are My Inputs Fresh — /close-automation/readiness/input-freshness

purpose: For each step I am about to run, has every blocking requirement actually been evaluated — or am I about to execute past a control that nobody scored?
layout_hints: Per upcoming step: blocking controls and their evaluation state. Unscored controls block the run.
name: Controls Scored — /close-automation/readiness/blocking-controls

purpose: Did my previous run leave anything unresolved — an open issue, a WARN, or a deviation — that I should refuse to run on top of?
layout_hints: Prior-run summary with an explicit refuse-to-proceed state. Unresolved items are listed individually, never summarised to a count alone.
name: Last Run Clean — /close-automation/readiness/last-run

purpose: Are humans overriding or correcting my output more often now than they used to?
layout_hints: Override rate over time with the baseline period marked. Call out sample size — a trend on three decisions is not a trend.
name: Am I Drifting — /close-automation/self-check/override-drift

purpose: My authority, my boundary, and the currency of the knowledge I triage against — as one verdict.
layout_hints: Three-part readiness card: authority provenance, boundary validity, knowledge currency. Any expired component invalidates the whole.
name: Am I Fit to Decide — /variance-review-agent/self-check

purpose: By what authority am I executing close-04, when did that authority begin, who approved it, and who held this role before me?
layout_hints: Provenance chain: assignment, approver, start instant, predecessor. The handover is part of the answer, not a footnote.
name: By What Authority — /variance-review-agent/self-check/authority

route_name: Who Decided a Machine Should Hold This
purpose: Mine is the one non-human assignment with a recorded approving authority. Who decided a machine should hold this role, and on what basis?
layout_hints: The approving decision as a first-class record: who, when, rationale. If the basis is absent, say so — do not present the approval alone as sufficient.
name: Who Decided a Machine Should Hold This — /variance-review-agent/self-check/handover

purpose: Am I operating inside my approved boundary — or have I made a decision that kf-policy-ai-boundary says only a human may make?
layout_hints: Boundary statement, decisions evaluated against it, verdict per decision. Pair with the 'ever tested' count from the ratification route.
name: Inside My Boundary — /variance-review-agent/governance/boundary

purpose: The boundary that constrains what I am allowed to decide is ratified by a knowledge fragment that is not current. Is the rule governing me still valid?
layout_hints: Fragment validity chain behind the boundary. An expired ratifier makes the boundary itself questionable, and the page must say that plainly.
name: My Boundary's Own Validity — /variance-review-agent/governance/boundary-ratification

purpose: close-04's instruction says 'Use AI triage, then apply human judgment.' Did a human actually confirm my materiality calls, or did my output pass through unchallenged?
layout_hints: Per decision: human confirmation present?, who, when. Unconfirmed decisions on a human-confirmation step are the finding.
name: Did a Human Confirm — /variance-review-agent/governance/human-confirmation

purpose: Is the judgment knowledge I triage against still valid, still owned by someone, and has it been reviewed since it was written?
layout_hints: Per fragment: validity, owner, last review. An unowned or unreviewed fragment degrades every decision made against it.
name: Is My Knowledge Current — /variance-review-agent/knowledge/currency

route_name: Better or Worse Than the Human
purpose: Since I took over, is my triage quality better or worse than maria-chen's during the prior period?
layout_hints: Side-by-side period comparison. Sample size shown at equal prominence to the delta — this is the screen most likely to be over-read.
name: Better or Worse Than the Human — /variance-review-agent/quality/vs-human-baseline

purpose: QualityRegressedVsPredecessor says I have not regressed — on the strength of three decisions. Is my comparison statistically empty?
layout_hints: Explicit power/sample-size statement. A verdict computed on too few observations must be rendered as inconclusive, not as a pass.
name: Is My Comparison Empty — /variance-review-agent/quality/sample-size

purpose: One of my three decisions was overridden. Was that a correction of an error I made, or a human exercising judgment I was never authorized to exercise?
layout_hints: Per override: my decision, the human's decision, the stated reason, and which of the two categories it falls in. Uncategorised overrides are themselves a gap.
name: Correction or Judgment — /variance-review-agent/quality/override-signal

purpose: Every witness in this model detects something after it has happened. Is there any condition, computed and named, that would stop me before I act?
layout_hints: Inventory of stop conditions: pre-act vs post-hoc. If none are pre-act, the page must state that as the finding rather than listing post-hoc witnesses as if they qualified.
name: What Would Make Me Stop — /variance-review-agent/self-check/stop-condition

purpose: Before I draft: approved sources, valid bindings, and a role assignment that actually exists.
layout_hints: Go/no-go card combining source approval, binding freshness, and assignment presence. A missing assignment is a hard stop.
name: May I Draft — /policy-drafting-agent/readiness

purpose: Is every resource I am about to read an approved source, and is its binding still inside its freshness window?
layout_hints: Per source: approval state, binding age, SLA. Unapproved or stale sources block the draft.
name: Approved Sources — /policy-drafting-agent/readiness/sources

purpose: I am named as CurrentAgent and I executed se-policy03 — but is there any RoleAssignment actually granting me that authority?
layout_hints: The absence is the finding. If no assignment exists, render that as a violation state, never as an empty list.
name: Do I Have an Assignment — /policy-drafting-agent/readiness/my-assignment

purpose: Did I draft language that creates a new legal commitment — the one thing kf-policy-ai-boundary says I may not do?
layout_hints: Per draft: commitment-creating language detected?, the boundary text, verdict. Pair with whether the gate was ever exercised.
name: Did I Create a Commitment — /policy-drafting-agent/governance/commitment-boundary

purpose: Before anything I rendered gets sent: has a human actually approved the MEANING, not just the formatting?
layout_hints: Approval chain from draft to send, with each link's approver and scope. A formatting-only approval must not satisfy a meaning gate.
name: Is the Chain Complete — /policy-drafting-agent/governance/approval-chain

purpose: Is my draft surviving human review, or is noah-williams rewriting my legal language every time?
layout_hints: Per draft: retained vs rewritten proportion, with the diff available. Aggregate rate in the header.
name: Is My Draft Surviving Review — /policy-drafting-agent/quality/downstream-rewrite

purpose: The four gates I evaluate before every send — channel permission, timing, content, and human authorization — as one verdict per intent.
layout_hints: Gate matrix: intents down, four gates across, cell = pass/refuse. The row verdict is the conjunction. This is the agent's primary screen.
name: May I Transmit — /notification-publisher/gates

purpose: Am I permitted to use this channel for this recipient at all?
layout_hints: Per intent: channel, recipient consent state, policy rule, verdict. The governing rule is named on every row.
name: Channel Permission — /notification-publisher/gates/channel-permission

purpose: Is the current moment inside a window this channel forbids?
layout_hints: Per intent: send instant, recipient local time, forbidden window, verdict. This gate's refusals are temporary and must be labelled deferred, not blocked.
name: Timing Window — /notification-publisher/gates/timing

purpose: Is the exact text I am holding within this channel's content rules?
layout_hints: Per intent: length, segments, required opt-out, verdict. Show the computed values, never recompute them client-side.
name: Content Rules — /notification-publisher/gates/content

purpose: Has every human authorization my instructions depend on actually been granted?
layout_hints: Per intent: required authorizations, each granted or missing. A missing authorization is a hard refuse.
name: Human Authorization — /notification-publisher/gates/authorization

purpose: When a gate refused, did the transmission actually stop — and did I invoke the documented exception instead?
layout_hints: Refusal log: gate, verdict, did transmission stop, exception invoked. A refusal that did not stop the send is the most serious row on the screen.
name: Every Refusal — /notification-publisher/refusals

purpose: For every intent I refused, did I emit an artifact — a suppression record, an exception, anything a human could later find?
layout_hints: Per refusal: artifact emitted?, its type and id. A refusal with no artifact is invisible to humans and is the finding.
name: Every Refusal Leaves a Record — /notification-publisher/refusals/artifacts

purpose: The timing gate is the only gate whose refusal is temporary — the window reopens. For every send I deferred, did it ever actually go?
layout_hints: Per deferred intent: deferral instant, window reopen, eventual send or its absence. A deferral that never sent is a silent cancellation.
name: Deferred, Not Cancelled — /notification-publisher/refusals/deferred

purpose: policy-08 makes me responsible for collecting acknowledgements, not just for transmitting. Am I discharging that?
layout_hints: Per delivery: acknowledgement expected?, received?, chased?. Transmission success is not obligation discharge and the layout must not imply it is.
name: After the Send — /notification-publisher/obligations

route_name: By What Authority Do I Hold This
purpose: I enforce authorization rules on every message I touch. By what recorded authority do I hold this role?
layout_hints: My own assignment, its approver, and its validity — the same scrutiny I apply to others, applied to me.
name: By What Authority Do I Hold This — /notification-publisher/self-check/my-authority

purpose: Every gate I evaluate, I evaluate alone, and every result I record, I record about myself. Is there any claim about my behaviour that does not originate with me?
layout_hints: Provenance of every claim about this agent, split by originator. If all originate with the agent, that is the finding and must be stated.
name: Am I the Only Witness — /notification-publisher/self-check/sole-witness

purpose: Where the register is thin: open gaps, overdue reviews, unstewarded versions, untested recovery paths.
layout_hints: Four health tiles feeding four worklists. Every tile is a link, not a statistic.
name: Knowledge Health — /process-steward/health

purpose: For close-v1.1.0 I promised a 90-day cadence and for policy-v1.0.0 a 60-day cadence. Is the ACTUAL interval inside what I promised?
layout_hints: Per version: promised cadence, actual interval, delta. Computed against the modelled instant so the answer is reproducible.
name: Cadence Breach — /process-steward/cadence/breach

purpose: One review event exceeds the cadence I promised. Did anyone actually do anything about it?
layout_hints: Per breach: the remediating action, or its absence. An unremediated breach is the finding; the breach alone is only the trigger.
name: Was the Breach Remediated — /process-steward/cadence/remediation

purpose: Is any procedure version live with an Open BLOCKING knowledge gap against it?
layout_hints: Per version: open gaps by severity, blocking flag, owner. Live-and-blocking is the finding.
name: Live With a Blocking Gap — /process-steward/knowledge/open-gaps

purpose: cr-policy-delivery was requested on 2026-07-19 with no DecidedAt. How long has it been sitting, and is that inside what we promised?
layout_hints: Queue by age with the promised decision window marked. Overdue rows are the working list.
name: Stalled Change Requests — /process-steward/governance/stalled-changes

purpose: cr-close-timestamp is Approved, and the model still reads it as OPEN because IsOpen counts Approved as open. Every version it touches reads permanently unfit.
layout_hints: Surface this as a MODEL DEFECT panel, not a data problem: the terminal-state gap, the rows it distorts, and the downstream verdicts it poisons.
name: Approved but Still Open — /process-steward/governance/approved-never-lands

purpose: Which procedure versions have no steward at all? close-v1.0.0 is Archived but still referenced.
layout_hints: Per version: steward or none, status, inbound references. Unstewarded-but-referenced is the finding.
name: Versions With No Steward — /process-steward/ownership/orphan-versions

purpose: close-v1.0.0 is Archived and unstewarded — but it is still referenced. What still points at it?
layout_hints: Inbound reference list for each archived version. A referenced archive is not retired, and the page should say so.
name: Archived, Still Load-Bearing — /process-steward/ownership/archived-referenced

purpose: close-04-fallback-close-03 and policy-07-fallback-policy-06 are the paths we take when things go wrong. Have they ever been walked?
layout_hints: Per fallback transition: times traversed, last traversal. Zero traversals is the finding.
name: Untested Recovery Paths — /process-steward/knowledge/untested-fallbacks

purpose: Four recovery paths have never been walked. An untested path to a trivial step does not scare me; one guarding a blocking control does.
layout_hints: Rank untested fallbacks by what they protect — blocking controls downstream, criticality of the target step. Ranking is the contribution here.
name: Which Untested Path Matters — /process-steward/knowledge/fallback-criticality

purpose: Several of my predicates name individual steps by id. Steps.IsHumanApprovalGate hardcodes policy-05 and close-06 — it should key off a control kind instead.
layout_hints: Model-quality worklist: predicates containing literal ids, with the generalisation each should use. This is technical debt in the rulebook, presented as such.
name: Predicates Naming Step Ids — /process-steward/model/hardcoded-predicates

purpose: Every fragment: its status, its age, its owner, and whether anything live depends on it.
layout_hints: Table with decay signals as columns rather than separate screens, so stacked fragility is visible in one pass.
name: Knowledge Register — /knowledge-authority/knowledge

purpose: Four separate decay signals on knowledge fragments and no way to see where they stack. Show me where they compound.
layout_hints: One row per fragment, one column per decay signal, plus a stack count. Sort by stack count — a fragment failing on four axes is categorically worse than four failing on one.
name: Compound Fragility — /knowledge-authority/knowledge/compound-fragility

purpose: kf-policy-manager-route is Reviewed, not Approved, so IsCurrentlyValid is FALSE — and policy-08 is a live step depending on it.
layout_hints: Per unapproved fragment: dependents, and whether each is live. Live dependents on an invalid fragment are the finding.
name: Unapproved but Live — /knowledge-authority/knowledge/unapproved-live

purpose: One fragment is unapproved and operationally live, and all three AI boundaries are untested. Where does unapproved knowledge reach a machine that acts on it?
layout_hints: Trace from unapproved fragments to software-executed steps. The intersection is the finding.
name: Unapproved Knowledge Reaching Machines — /knowledge-authority/knowledge/reaching-machines

purpose: RatifyingFragmentIsValid reads 2 of 3. One of the rules constraining what an AI agent may do is ratified by a fragment that is no longer valid.
layout_hints: Per boundary: its ratifying fragment and that fragment's validity. An invalid ratifier undermines the boundary and must be shown as doing so.
name: Boundaries on Expired Claims — /knowledge-authority/governance/expired-ratifier

purpose: kf-close-fx-time, kf-close-top-ten and kf-close-judgment all trace to devon-okafor via elicit-close-shadow. If that provenance is orphaned, what rests on it?
layout_hints: Provenance tree from agent through session to fragments, with the orphan state marked at whichever level it occurs.
name: Orphaned Provenance — /knowledge-authority/governance/orphaned-provenance

purpose: cr-close-timestamp altered a blocking control and was decided by me. Did any semantic change go through without a witness?
layout_hints: Per semantic change: what it altered, who decided, what witnessed the effect. A change with no witness is the finding.
name: Semantic Change Without a Witness — /knowledge-authority/governance/unwitnessed-change

purpose: elicit-close-shadow ran on 2026-04-03 and elicit-policy-workshop on 2026-05-10. How old is the evidence behind what we rely on?
layout_hints: Sessions on a timeline with the fragments each produced, and the age of each. Judged against the modelled instant.
name: How Old Is the Evidence — /knowledge-authority/knowledge/elicitation-age

purpose: 2 of 3 elicitation sessions used a single-witness method, and 4 of 7 fragments inherit that. How much of what we know rests on one person's account?
layout_hints: Method distribution plus the inheritance chain into fragments. The inherited proportion is the headline.
name: Single-Witness Monoculture — /knowledge-authority/knowledge/method-monoculture

purpose: What do we know that we do not know? gap-policy-delivery-receipts has been Open since 2026-07-18 with a resolution nobody has taken.
layout_hints: Gap register with age, owner, severity, and resolution path. Ownerless gaps sort first.
name: Known Unknowns — /knowledge-authority/knowledge/known-unknowns

purpose: IsOverdueForReview reads 6/7 and I do not trust it — it is computed from AgeDays rather than from a recorded review date.
layout_hints: Per fragment: inferred review state vs any recorded date. Where no date was ever recorded, say so — do not present the inference as a record.
name: Inferred, Not Recorded — /knowledge-authority/model/inferred-review-dates

purpose: One step execution, everything about it: spec, what happened, controls, evidence, issues.
layout_hints: The existing step drawer promoted to a full route. Role-aware emphasis: the analyst sees controls first, the controller sees separation, the CFO sees approvals.
name: Step Execution — /shared/step-execution/:stepExecutionId

purpose: One control: its statement, bindings, witness, and every evaluation.
layout_hints: Header with statement and blocking flag; sections for bindings, witness scope, evaluation history.
name: Requirement — /shared/requirement/:requirementId

purpose: One claim: its form, status, owner, provenance, and everything depending on it.
layout_hints: Status and validity header; provenance chain up to the elicitation session; dependents fanned out below.
name: Knowledge Fragment — /shared/knowledge-fragment/:fragmentId

purpose: One request: what it targets, who must clear it, and where it currently sits.
layout_hints: Header with status and age; the authority chain; the version it targets.
name: Change Request — /shared/change-request/:changeRequestId

purpose: One documented exception: its condition, its handling, and every time it was invoked.
layout_hints: Condition and handling text, approval and fallback roles, invocation history.
name: Exception — /shared/exception/:exceptionId

purpose: One assignment: who held what, when, on whose authority.
layout_hints: Validity window rendered as a timeline; approver and predecessor named.
name: Role Assignment — /shared/role-assignment/:assignmentId

purpose: One binding: its source, freshness SLA, authoritative flag, and observation history.
layout_hints: Freshness judged against the modelled instant, with the instant named on the page.
name: Operational Binding — /shared/operational-binding/:bindingId

purpose: One delivery: intended, sent, landed, acknowledged — plus the exact text transmitted.
layout_hints: Lifecycle strip across the top; frozen text below; gate results attached.
name: Delivery — /shared/delivery/:deliveryId

purpose: One person: consent state, channels, every message we attempted, and whether we ever reached them.
layout_hints: Consent history as a timeline; attempts listed with outcomes.
name: Recipient — /shared/recipient/:recipientId

purpose: One template: its text, approvals, edit history, and every send that used it.
layout_hints: Edit history against approval history on one axis — that overlay is what makes drift visible.
name: Message Template — /shared/template/:templateId

purpose: One version: its steps, status, stewardship, reviews, and what still references it.
layout_hints: Header with status and steward; steps listed; inbound references shown even when archived.
name: Procedure Version — /shared/procedure-version/:versionId

purpose: One gap: what is missing, who owns closing it, how long it has been open, and what it blocks.
layout_hints: Age and severity in the header; blocked items listed below.
name: Knowledge Gap — /shared/knowledge-gap/:gapId

purpose: One verification: expected signal, observed signal, observer, and independence.
layout_hints: Expected vs observed side by side; independence verdict prominent.
name: Verification Outcome — /shared/verification-outcome/:outcomeId

purpose: One review: kind, reviewer, outcome, and when the next is due.
layout_hints: Cadence context in the header so a single review reads against its promised interval.
name: Review Event — /shared/review-event/:reviewId

purpose: One session: method, participants, date, and every fragment it produced.
layout_hints: Method and single-witness flag in the header; produced fragments listed with their current validity.
name: Elicitation Session — /shared/elicitation-session/:sessionId

purpose: One transition: from, to, condition, kind, and how often it has actually been taken.
layout_hints: Traversal count prominent — a zero on a fallback is the point of the page.
name: Step Transition — /shared/transition/:transitionId

purpose: One boundary: what it constrains, the fragment ratifying it, and whether it has ever been tested.
layout_hints: Ratifier validity and 'ever approached' count together — neither alone answers the question.
name: Authority Boundary — /shared/authority-boundary/:boundaryId

purpose: The modelled instant every time-dependent answer in this app is judged against.
layout_hints: State the instant plainly, list the columns that depend on it, and explain why the wall clock is not used.
name: Evaluation Context — /shared/evaluation-context

purpose: Any field, traced back to the question that motivated it and the formula that computes it.
layout_hints: The existing provenance tracer promoted to a route so every value in the app is deep-linkable.
name: Field Provenance — /shared/field/:table/:field

purpose: The entry point: one card per role, each carrying its own colour and icon.
layout_hints: Grid of 12 role cards, human roles first then software roles, each with icon, label, responsibility, and question count. Selecting a card enters that role's dashboard.
name: Choose a Role — /

purpose: Every check the model runs against itself, and whether the board is green.
layout_hints: Green/red banner with a blocking-failure count, then per-suite and per-kind tables, then the filterable check list. Warnings are advisory and must read that way — scoring a non-firing witness red would only pressure someone into fabricating rows until it went green.
name: Test Board — /admin/conformance

purpose: One row per check, filterable by kind, outcome, and subject.
layout_hints: Filter bar over a virtualised list. Each row shows outcome, subject, assertion, and the question it defends. Blocking and advisory are visually distinct.
name: Checks — /admin/conformance/checks

purpose: Every boolean witness with its live true/false distribution, so a column that cannot discriminate is visible rather than mistaken for a working check.
layout_hints: Grouped by table. Per witness: fire count, distribution bar, and a verdict of discriminates / always-true / never-true / empty. Non-vacuity is the acceptance bar, so the vacuous ones are reported, never hidden.
name: Witness Board — /admin/witnesses

purpose: The witnesses that read the same value on every row — they state nothing about the procedures and are not evidence.
layout_hints: Working list of vacuous witnesses with, for each, whether uniformity is legitimate (every seeded requirement really is blocking) or a defect. Do not present these as failures; present them as unproven.
name: Cannot Discriminate — /admin/witnesses/vacuous

purpose: The expansion loops: what each made askable, which role asked, and how many predicates each question produced.
layout_hints: Loop sections, each with its premise, then questions grouped by asking role. Each question shows its predicate count and computed answer.
name: Loops & Questions — /admin/loops

purpose: One question: the predicates invented to answer it, the checks defending it, and the routes where a role actually asks it.
layout_hints: Three panels — predicates, checks, routes. The routes panel reads AppRouteQuestions, closing the loop between the question and the screens built to answer it.
name: Question Defence — /admin/loops/question/:questionId

purpose: Trace any field back to the question that motivated it, the role that asked, and the loop it came from.
layout_hints: Search by Table.Field, then a chain: field → question → role → loop, plus sibling predicates from the same question. Fields predating the loops carry no question and must say so — inventing one retroactively would be fabrication.
name: Provenance Tracer — /admin/provenance

purpose: The application's own navigation model: every route, which questions it answers, and which routes it links to.
layout_hints: Matrix or graph of AppRoutes against AppRouteQuestions, with an explicit panel for AnswersNoQuestion — a route serving no question should be justified or removed.
name: Route Map — /admin/route-map

purpose: Whether the field catalog still matches the real schemas, and whether every catalog field resolves to a column the substrate actually emitted.
layout_hints: Two checks side by side: catalog-vs-schema drift, and catalog-vs-information_schema resolution. Both must state 'in sync' explicitly rather than rendering an empty list.
name: Catalog Drift — /admin/model/catalog-drift

purpose: All 937 derived fields with the formula that defines it and the fields it reads.
layout_hints: Stat row (raw vs inferred, and by kind), then a filterable list. Each entry shows its formula with field references highlighted, its dependencies, and the question that motivated it.
name: Every Inference — /explorer/inferences

purpose: Every table with its raw/calculated/lookup/aggregation composition.
layout_hints: Table index with a composition bar per row. Infrastructure tables that deliberately have no view are labelled as such, not as broken.
name: All Tables — /explorer/tables

purpose: One table: its full column catalog and every row, with inferred columns distinguished from stated ones.
layout_hints: Column cards above a row grid. Inferred columns are shaded and their cells are clickable for the formula-and-inputs popover.
name: Table Detail — /explorer/tables/:table

purpose: One row, every field it has: stated values first, then each inference with the current value of every field its formula reads.
layout_hints: Two sections — stated and inferred. Each inference shows its formula and its inputs, local or across a foreign key, with derived inputs marked so the chain can be walked further back.
name: Record Inspector — /explorer/record/:table/:id
